title: Weighted flags, monomial bases and minimum Hilbert weight
statement: Let $k$ be a field [def-weil-field], $r=n+2\geq2$, and $i:X\to\mathbf P^{r-1}_k$ a morphism of schemes [def-pc-scheme], using the standard projective space [def-nagata-projective-space-base-change] and the coordinate index of [lem-sfb-hilbert-plucker-pgl-linearization]. Let $V=k[x_1,\ldots,x_r]_1$ be the degree-one homogeneous subspace of the polynomial ring [def-weil-pbc-mv-polynomial-ring]. Put $H_m=H^0(X,i^*\mathcal O(m))$ [def-pc-projective-space-twist], [def-pc-module-pullback], [def-sc-ringed-space-module-cohomology], with scalars restricted along the structural map to $\operatorname{Spec}k$, as in [lem-sfb-uniform-projective-fibre-vanishing]. Given a basis $b=(b_j)$ of $V$ and weights $w_j\in\mathbf N$, define its increasing weighted flag by $F_s=\operatorname{span}_k\{b_j:w_j\leq s\}$ for $s\in\mathbf N$. For $m\in\mathbf N$ and an exponent vector $e\in\mathbf N^r$ with $\sum_j e_j=m$, define $b^e=\prod_j b_j^{e_j}\in k[x_1,\ldots,x_r]_m$ (constructed by homogeneous projection, which fixes this product). Given a $k$-linear arrow $\rho:k[x_1,\ldots,x_r]_m\to H_m$, a finite set $S$ of such exponent vectors is a monomial basis if $(\rho(b^e))_{e\in S}$ is linearly independent and spans $H_m$. Define $W_w(S)=\sum_{e\in S}\sum_j w_j e_j$ and $w_{\rho,b,w}(m)=\inf\{W_w(S):S\text{ is a monomial basis}\}\in\mathbf N$, where $\inf\varnothing=0$ is the totalized natural-number infimum convention. When a monomial basis exists this infimum is the attained minimum; no existence assertion is part of this definition.
